latestRelease.notes:
## v0.21.8 - 2026-07-29

### Changed

- Changeset diffs are now computed from filesystem metadata instead of full-content comparison, significantly speeding up diff computation for large directories. by @marcosnils in
  https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13615

### Fixed

- Dockerfile build layer caching so unrelated build-context changes no longer bust the cache: `COPY`-ed directories now get a content-based cache identity, re-keying downstream steps only when copied content
  actually changes. by @marcosnils in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13765
- The `--x-release` CLI re-exec so `_EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST` is preserved (with a warning) instead of being stripped, and clarified its startup message to avoid implying it runs from any build. by
  @tiborvass in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13752
- Silent SDK sessions no longer retain frontend telemetry in memory while Cloud and OTLP export remain enabled. `DAGGER_SILENT` is now honored as the equivalent of `--silent`. by @sipsma in
  https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13762

### What to do next?

- Read the [documentation](https://docs.dagger.io)
- Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/dagger-io)
- Follow us on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/dagger_io)

signals.title: 🐞 `withRegistryAuth` invalidates image and execution caches across sessions
signals.text: ### What is the issue? `Container.withRegistryAuth` changes the cache identity of an otherwise unchanged container. Image pulls and downstream executions then miss the cache across Dagger sessions. Registry credentials are session state and are not stored in `core.Container`. Therefore, adding credentials should not change the container filesystem or invalidate downstream execution cache entries. The problem occurs even when the configured registry address is unrelated to the image being pulled: ```go client.Container(). WithRegistryAuth("registry.example.com", "anyuser", secret). From("alpine:3.20"). WithExec(...) ``` The same execution without `WithRegistryAuth` is cached across sessions. The authenticated branch runs again and produces a different random value. This reproduces with Dagger v0.21.8, v1.0.0-beta.9, and current `main` at `b068d8a7b`. The original user report is in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/707636530424053791/1488136596237713459/1537636243314049065). #### Expected `withRegistryAuth` registers credentials in the current session without changing the identity of the returned container. If the resolved image digest and execution inputs are unchanged, image and execution cache entries should be reusable across sessions. #### Actual The authenticated branch has a different identity in every session. The digest-qualified `Container.from` operation runs instead of reporting `CACHED`, a nested pull span appears, and downstream `withExec` runs again. #### Root cause `withRegistryAuth` is registered with `dagql.PerSessionInput`. Its resolver mutates the session authentication provider and returns the unchanged Go container pointer. However, `dagql.Func` wraps that pointer in a new result whose recipe contains the session ID. That session-scoped result becomes the receiver of `Container.from` and all later operations. It also prevents the canonical `From` path from assigning its stable image content identity because the direct parent call is `withRegistryAuth`, not the bare `container` call. The behavior was introduced by `3fde468ad` and first appeared in v0.21.1. That change fixed a real problem where the authentication side effect could be skipped in a new session, but it coupled session-local side-effect execution to the semantic identity of the returned container. `withoutRegistryAuth` has the same identity and mutable-side-effect concerns. #### Suggested fix Treat `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth` as non-cacheable session operations while returning the attached parent container result. This keeps explicit credential mutations ordered and ensures that registry authentication does not become part of the container identity. ### Dagger version ```text dagger v0.21.8 (image://registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.8) linux/amd64 ``` Also reproduced with: ```text client-version=v1.0.0-beta.9 server-version=v1.0.0-beta.9+1c6e07b1 ``` ### Steps to reproduce Create a Go program using `dagger.io/dagger v0.21.8`: ```go package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "strings" "dagger.io/dagger" ) func main() { ctx := context.Background() client, err := dagger.Connect(ctx, dagger.WithLogOutput(os.Stderr)) if err != nil { panic(err) } defer client.Close() stamp := []string{"sh", "-c", "cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid > /stamp; cat /stamp"} control := client.Container(). From("alpine:3.20"). WithExec(stamp) bug := client.Container(). WithRegistryAuth( "registry.example.com", "anyuser", client.SetSecret("s", "dummy"), ). From("alpine:3.20"). WithExec(stamp) controlStamp, err := control.File("/stamp").Contents(ctx) if err != nil { panic(err) } bugStamp, err := bug.File("/stamp").Contents(ctx) if err != nil { panic(err) } fmt.Println("CONTROL", strings.TrimSpace(controlStamp)) fmt.Println("BUG ", strings.TrimSpace(bugStamp)) } ``` Run it in two separate sessions: ```shell go mod init registry-auth-cache-repro go get dagger.io/dagger@v0.21.8 go run . go run . ``` To test v1.0.0-beta.9, add this connection option and run the program directly: ```go dagger.WithEnvironmentVariable("DAGGER_X_RELEASE", "v1.0.0-beta.9") ``` ### Log output ```text Session 1 CONTROL 3c58afe2-abf3-4aa3-90a3-ec5c0f381c70 BUG cb70c53c-12ae-413a-9b16-892d34178fbd Session 2 CONTROL 3c58afe2-abf3-4aa3-90a3-ec5c0f381c70 BUG 10087caa-e917-4062-aebe-f761d87a14be ``` Verbose spans show the difference: ```text # Control branch Container.from CACHED Container.withExec CACHED # withRegistryAuth branch, in both sessions pulling docker.io/library/alpine:3.20@sha256:... DONE Container.from DONE Container.withExec DONE ```

signals.title: How do we support workspace configs that arent at the repo root
signals.text: Related issues: - https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13890 - https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13892 - https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13893 - https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13882 We currently have a few assumptions that the Workspace config (dagger.toml) is at the repository root. At one point in the Workspace design, we talked about nested Workspace configs, but that was cut for now because of the complexity it adds. The question is, if we do support dagger.toml placed somewhere other than the repo root, how do we support that - How does Cloud Checks determine the correct config location? - If there are multiple configs, how do we select one? - Are paths in the config always from the repo root or workspace config?

signals.title: Clean up tests for the Go client library
signals.text: ## Problem To test the Go client library, we built a custom test harness. That harness only runs in GitHub Actions; it relies heavily on single-use glue code; and it jams together testing dimensions that should be decoupled. Concretely: the `TestProvision` test is wired into `publish.yml` and only runs on pushes to main and tags, never on a PR. The rest of the suite runs through `go-sdk-dev`, a Dagger module built only to call `go test`. And one suite does three jobs at once — bootstrap the CLI, start an engine, test the client — so a developer with plain `go test` can't run any of it. ## Solution Turn them into ordinary Go tests. The engine-dependent tests move to `sdk/go/e2e`, a normal Go module which can be tested by `go test`, either called directly by the user, or orchestrated by a generic Dagger module such as `github.com/dagger/go`. | Dependency | Before | After | | -- | -- | -- | | Github Actions | required 🔴 | not required 🟢 | | Single-use Dagger module | required 🔴 | not required 🟢 | | Run with native `go test` | not supported 🔴 | supported 🟢 | - `sdk/go` holds unit tests with no engine dependency, and pre-existing documentation examples. - `sdk/go/e2e` holds two e2e test suites: `TestBootstrap` (the library downloads and runs a CLI), and `TestAgainstEngines` (call the library against a matrix of engines) ## Task list > **TL;DR:** `sdk/go/e2e`'s `TestBootstrap` and `TestAgainstEngines` both fail during their shared harness setup. The nested Dagger client detects the container's projected filesystem as its workspace instead of inheriting the caller's workspace. - [ ] Fix both tests by implementing [#13054](https://github.com/dagger/dagger/issues/13054).

signals.title: core: pin latest container and Git releases
signals.text: ## Summary Implement #13464's package-manager-style latest-release lifecycle for Git repositories and container images. For Git: - add `GitRepository.latest` - select the greatest stable semantic-version tag, accepting both `v1.2.3` and `1.2.3` - ignore prerelease tags - fall back to the resolved remote HEAD when no stable release tag exists - load remote metadata lazily so frozen pins do not contact the remote For containers: - treat a bare image address such as `alpine` as a latest-release lookup - select the greatest stable semantic-version tag - ignore prerelease tags - fall back to the literal `latest` tag when no stable release tag exists - keep explicit tags such as `alpine:latest` and `alpine:3.22`, plus digested references, on the existing exact-resolution path - list registry tags using the existing authentication, mirror, network, protocol, and TLS settings ## Lockfile behavior The operations intentionally have different lock formats: | Operation | Inputs | Pin value | | --- | --- | --- | | `git.latest` | remote URL | selected symbolic ref and commit as `ref@commit` | | `container.from.latest` | normalized bare repository, platform, and optional transport settings | selected tag and digest as `tag@digest` | | `container.from` | explicit tagged reference, platform, and optional transport settings | resolved digest | All latest-release entries use pin policy. Pinned and frozen resolution reuse the stored selection instead of listing Git refs or container tags again. For example: - `git.latest`: `refs/tags/v0.21.4@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567` - `container.from.latest`: `docker.io/library/alpine:3.22.1@sha256:...` - `container.from` for `alpine:latest`: `sha256:...` ## `dagger update` `dagger update` refreshes existing lock entries in place: - `git.latest` reloads the remote refs, selects the latest stable release again, and stores its current commit - `container.from.latest` relists registry tags, selects the latest stable release again, and stores its current digest - exact `container.from` entries resolve the explicit tag again and refresh its digest - container updates preserve optional HTTP/HTTPS and `insecureSkipTLSVerify` lock inputs The update operation does not need the previous pin to resolve successfully; it derives a replacement from the lock entry's operation and inputs. ## Status - [x] Implement latest-release selection and lock lifecycle for Git - [x] Implement latest-release selection and lock lifecycle for containers - [x] Keep explicit container tags and digests on exact `container.from` - [x] Support live, pinned, frozen, and update workflows - [x] Avoid eager Git remote metadata access in frozen mode - [x] Regenerate SDK clients and references for `GitRepository.latest` No container SDK regeneration is needed because the container behavior does not add or change a public GraphQL field. ## How to test Run the focused unit and schema tests: ```console go test ./core ./core/schema ./engine/server/resolver go test ./core/integration -run '^$' ``` Run the lock lifecycle tests against a development engine: ```console dagger api call engine-dev test \ --pkg ./core/integration \ --run='TestLockfile/(TestGitLatestLiveCreatesPin|TestGitLatestFrozenUsesPin|TestGitLatestFrozenDoesNotLoadRemoteMetadata|TestUpdateRefreshesExistingGitLatestEntry|TestContainerFromLatestLockLifecycle|TestFromLockfileLiveRefreshesEntry|TestLockUpdateRefreshesExistingEntry)$' ``` For a manual check, save this as `latest.graphql` in a workspace: ```graphql { git(url: "https://github.com/dagger/dagger.git") { latest { ref commit } } container { latestRelease: from(address: "alpine") { imageRef } explicitLatest: from(address: "alpine:latest") { imageRef } } } ``` Then exercise the lifecycle: ```console dagger --lock=live query --doc latest.graphql cat dagger.lock dagger --lock=frozen query --doc latest.graphql dagger update cat dagger.lock ``` The lockfile should contain `git.latest`, `container.from.latest`, and `container.from` entries with the formats described above.

signals.title: dagger agent dev env: in-repo agent modules
signals.text: The dogfooding layer: the in-repo agent modules that `dagger agent --env dev` composes, plus the wiring that makes them reachable. No engine changes. | module | what it does | | --- | --- | | `editor` | a sandboxed coding agent — read, write, edit, find, grep, todoWrite — plus a commit tool built on the workspace's staged commits. Vendored from `github.com/vito/editor` so it can be iterated on in-tree. | | `review` | the `git status` / `git diff` an agent with no Bash tool can't otherwise get, via `Workspace.git.uncommitted`'s diffstats and patch | | `history` | the `git log` half of the same, over `Workspace.git.stagedCommits` | | `delegate` | hands a noisy, context-heavy subtask to a fresh sub-agent that runs it in its own conversation and returns one distilled report | | `engine-lab` | `./hack/dev` + `./hack/with-dev` as agent tools: build from the workspace, hold the engine as a Service, exec against it, poke its debug endpoints | | `contributor` | the same idea aimed at somebody else's repo — fetch it as a Workspace, compose editor's tools onto it, work the task, open the PR | | `tui-qa` | drives nested agent TUI sessions; now inherits the session's LLM config and gets a real git repo as its fixture | Supporting changes: `EngineDev.GoContainer` is a Wolfi Go base with the from-source `dagger` on `$PATH`, so Go commands (and the integration tests, which shell out to `dagger`) find the CLI without paying for a full engine build — it's what the `golang` toolchain is based on in the dev env. `dagger.toml` gains the `env.dev` module set, with contributor's GitHub token resolving through `cmd://gh auth token` rather than being stored. And catwalk moves to v0.51.11 for its refreshed model catalog. Each module commit is self-contained, and the `dagger.toml` wiring is last, so any intermediate state is a module directory with no install entry — inert rather than broken.

signals.title: workspace: add native polyfill replacements
signals.text: `dagger/polyfill` currently provides two pieces of workspace logic that belong in the engine. This PR adds their native replacements without changing how changesets work. `Workspace.findRoots` finds projects from marker files such as `go.mod` or `package.json`. It searches below the workspace cwd, includes the nearest enclosing project, and prunes excluded trees. `glob` remains the lower-level API for callers that only need path matching. SDKs do not need to scan the filesystem for Dagger modules. Those modules are already registered in `dagger.toml`, so `currentModule.asSDK(workspace: ws).modules` returns the registered module objects relevant to the workspace cwd. The PR also preserves a literal `engineVersion: "latest"` when editing module configuration and adds the missing regression test for loading local dependencies through `Workspace.moduleSource`. #### Review The main question is the API boundary: `findRoots` discovers ordinary projects from files, while `asSDK.modules` reads the Dagger modules already registered for that SDK. #### Test ```console go test ./core ./core/schema dagger call engine-dev test --run 'TestWorkspaceFindRoots|TestEngineVersionLatestStaysFloating|TestContextualWorkspaceModuleSourceLocalDeps' ``` [#13855](https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13855) builds on this with workspace generation and explicit changeset comparison.

signals.title: workspace: compare changes from an explicit baseline
signals.text: This completes the engine API needed to remove `dagger/polyfill`. The caller now keeps the workspace it received, generates files on a new immutable workspace value, then compares the two: ```text before = disk + existing edits after = moduleSource.generate(before) # before + generated files after.changes(from: before) # generated files only ``` `ModuleSource.generate(workspace)` returns a `Workspace`, so SDKs can compose generation with normal workspace edits. `Workspace.changes(from:)` performs the comparison only when a `Changeset` is required and returns paths relative to the workspace cwd. This avoids a separate `WorkspaceDiff` type and avoids a `fork()` lifecycle that callers could forget. The baseline is an ordinary immutable workspace value already available to the caller. It also handles module initialization correctly: the SDK sees the staged module scaffold, but returns only the files it generated. `ModuleSource.generateLocalDependencies` remains temporarily because released SDKs still call it. New SDK code uses `generate`; the compatibility field can be removed after those migrations ship. This PR builds on [#13854](https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13854). #### Test ```console go test ./core ./core/schema dagger call engine-dev test --run 'TestWorkspaceChangesFrom|TestWorkspaceChangesetRooting|TestModuleInitGeneratesForNewModuleOnly|TestGenerateLocalDependenciesTerminatesOnRootDep|TestGeneratorsInstalledInWorkspace' ```

signals.title: sdk(improvement): support nullable object returns
signals.text: #### What Support nullable GraphQL object results in generated clients and built-in module SDKs. The motivating API is `GitRepository.latestVersion`: a repository may have no stable semantic-version tag, so callers need a real missing value and can choose a fallback. ```go version, err := repo.LatestVersion(ctx) if err != nil { return err } if version == nil { version = repo.Head() } ``` #### Generated clients Nullable object methods now query the object's ID before returning. A missing ID becomes the language's native empty value; a present ID rebuilds the object client. Non-null object fields stay lazy, and scalar and list methods do not change. This produces `nil` in Go, `null` in TypeScript, PHP, and .NET, `None` or `Option` in Python and Rust, `Optional` in Java, and `{:ok, value | nil}` in Elixir. #### Module functions Module authors can also declare nullable object returns: - TypeScript: `Promise<User | null>` - PHP: `?Directory` - Java: `Optional<Directory>` - Go: `dagger.Nullable[*dagger.Directory]` Python and Dang already had nullable syntax. This also completes Elixir's existing `Object.t() | nil` path by registering and encoding optional object results correctly. #### Compatibility and tests Generated templates receive the schema version and keep the old lazy method shape before `v1.0.0-beta.10`. From beta.10 onward, nullable object methods use the new eager nullable result. This preserves modules pinned to older schemas without adding runtime compatibility code. Generator tests cover both sides of the version boundary. Runtime integration tests exercise both a present object and `null` for Go, TypeScript, PHP, Java, Python, and Elixir. Focused SDK tests and lint pass locally with the pinned beta.10 release.

signals.title: feat(workspace): build a workspace on another workspace's config
signals.text: ## What Adds a top-level `blueprint` key to `dagger.toml`: a Git ref to the workspace this one builds on, whose configuration is merged **underneath** the current one. ```toml blueprint = "github.com/acme/dagger-base@v1.2.0" # Only the difference from the blueprint: [modules.go.settings] goVersion = "1.24" ``` A team can publish one base workspace config — shared tool versions, module refs, settings, environments — and have many downstream repos point at it instead of copying it into each one. Asked for on Discord (vindico: "I'm currently putting duplicated workspace config in a lot of repos"; chrisp6229 asked for exactly this, per project type), and scoped to shykes' "as long as we don't go crazy with the config layering... a basic import feature in dagger.toml". Design doc and implementation plan: `future/done/workspace-blueprint.md`. ## Merge semantics The workspace naming the blueprint wins every conflict. Layering, lowest first: the blueprint's `dagger.toml` → this repo's `dagger.toml` → user-level overrides → `--env` overlay. Nothing about the existing three layers changes. - **Module entries merge per field**, so a repo can override one setting without repeating the module's ref. That makes `source` optional in the file — an entry may be a pure override of a module the blueprint installs. - **"Set" means explicitly present**, not non-zero: `entrypoint = false` and `ignore = []` override an inherited value. Presence comes from the raw TOML, not the parsed struct. - `as-sdk` and `legacy-default-path` are **never inherited** — both describe the blueprint's own tree. - `[ports.<host>]` replaces the inherited mapping as a unit. - Envs merge by name; an env only the blueprint defines is selectable downstream. The full per-section table is in the design doc. ## The two deliberate limits 1. **One blueprint, no chain.** A `blueprint` in the blueprint's own config is an error, not a second layer. Ignoring it would hand the user a config silently missing whatever the blueprint author expected to inherit. 2. **Only remote modules.** Module entries in the blueprint whose source is a local path are dropped, with a warning naming them, before the merge — along with their env overlays and any port mapping that forwards to them. Dropping rather than erroring, because a normal repo keeps its own modules under `modules/`, and erroring would make ordinary repos unusable as blueprints. (See the note below — this limit is the one worth revisiting.) Classification of "local" is `gitref.FastKindCheck(source, "")` plus a directory stat **in the blueprint tree**, deliberately not `core.ParseRefString`: - an entry's own pin must not be passed, because any non-empty pin makes `FastKindCheck` return `KindGit` while the module loader classifies without it — `source = "./ci", pin = "…"` would otherwise pass as remote and then resolve locally; - `ParseRefString` falls back to *local* on `gitref.EndpointError`, so a vanity-domain remote would be dropped whenever endpoint discovery is unavailable. Classification must not depend on network reachability. Without the drop, an inherited `source = "modules/ci"` resolves against the **consuming** workspace's config dir — loading a different module, or failing with a path the user never wrote. The integration test asserts exactly that case, with a same-named directory present downstream. ## Lockfile No new lock entry kind. The blueprint resolves through the ordinary `git(url).head` / `.ref(name)` selectors, so it records the standard `git.ref` / `git.head` entry in `dagger.lock`: `dagger update` and `--lock=live` refresh it, `--lock=frozen` replays the pin and fails when it is missing. Resolution runs after the client's workspace is bound, which is what puts the entry in the right lockfile. ## Reads are effective, writes are local `readWorkspaceConfig` — behind module/env/SDK listings and `currentModule.asSDK` — returns the merged config, as does `configRead`, **including its base path**, which is the plain `dagger workspace config` case and returns raw bytes today. `--load-module <name>` resolves the blueprint's modules too. The no-argument output is a standalone snapshot: the `blueprint` key is stripped and named in a `# blueprint: <ref>` comment, the same way the env-effective view already clears `Env`. Keeping it would make the printed config one that inlines the inherited values *and* names the blueprint again underneath. `dagger workspace config blueprint` still reports the local value. Writes never touch the blueprint's config, and now say so when that would be confusing: unsetting a value the blueprint supplies names the blueprint instead of reporting that nothing is set. `dagger uninstall` on a module that exists only in the blueprint says it cannot be uninstalled here; on a source-less override it removes the override and reports that the module is still provided by the blueprint. Installing over a source-less override fills in its source (and clears the pin that belonged to the inherited ref) rather than reporting a conflict. ## Naming The key is `blueprint`, not `import`. The word has history here: legacy `dagger.json` had a `blueprint` field naming the module that defined a project's pipeline, retired by the workspace migration in favour of `entrypoint = true`, and `dagger-module.toml` still rejects the field outright. Reusing it is deliberate — same idea one level up, a base *workspace configuration* rather than a base *module*. The reference docs say plainly what the workspace `blueprint` is not, and nothing in the legacy path changes. ## Judgment calls worth a second opinion - **Scalar `blueprint` rather than `[blueprint] source = "…"`.** One field, the pin lives in `dagger.lock`, and "basic import feature" was the brief — but it is a one-way door if a second field is ever wanted. - **`ModuleEntry.Source` gains `omitempty`**, so the generated JSON schema no longer marks it required. `ValidateEffectiveConfig` replaces that check on the *effective* config and runs whether or not a blueprint is present — stronger than the schema rule it replaces, but it means a config with a source-less module entry, which loads (uselessly) on main today, now fails. Port mappings are deliberately *not* validated: `dagger workspace config ports.3000.backendService web` writes one key while the serializer writes both, so a partial mapping is a state the CLI itself produces. - **Residual sanitization hole, documented not closed**: a blueprint source that is `KindUnknown`, absent from the blueprint tree, and present as a directory in the consuming tree is kept and resolves locally. It needs a base config whose own entry is already unloadable plus a colliding downstream directory; closing it means threading a "resolve remotely only" hint through `moduleSource`, which is a resolution-pipeline change rather than a config feature. - **No tombstones.** An inherited entry can be overridden but not deleted. - **Lock refresh is not covered by a new integration test**: moving the served base branch under the same URL is not expressible with the git-service fixture, and the entry is the ordinary `git.ref` entry whose refresh `lockfile_test.go` already covers. ## Patches | Patch | Scope | | --- | --- | | `workspace-blueprint-config` | `core/workspace`: the key, presence detection, pure merge, `ValidateEffectiveConfig` | | `workspace-blueprint-resolve` | `core`: shared remote-workspace resolution, blueprint loading and sanitization | | `workspace-blueprint-load` | `engine/server`: merge during workspace load | | `workspace-blueprint-reads` | `core/schema`: effective reads, patch-entry-aware install/uninstall | | `workspace-blueprint-tests` | `core/integration`: multi-workspace fixture over a git service | | `workspace-blueprint-docs` | reference page, regenerated schema, changelog, CLI help | Design doc and plan are the first patches in the series. ## Follow-up under consideration: the blueprint's own modules Limit 2 (local modules dropped) is worth revisiting, and the mechanism is already in the tree. Because the blueprint *is* a git ref, its local modules are addressable as refs into the same repository at the same commit — which is exactly what `-W <git ref>` already does for remote workspaces (`resolveLocalRef` → `core.GitRefString`). Rewriting `source = "modules/ci"` into `<clone-ref>/modules/ci@<resolved-sha>` instead of dropping it has been verified to load end-to-end against a dev engine, keeps the config and its modules commit-closed, and adds no per-module lock entries (a 40-char SHA short-circuits the lock lookup). Two prerequisites found while investigating, both pre-existing: `gitref.Parse` drops an explicit HTTP(S) port when rebuilding the clone ref, and `GitRefString` silently normalizes an escaping subpath (`../outside` → `/outside`) instead of rejecting it. Built-in SDK pseudo-sources (`source = "php"`), `as-sdk` paths, `legacy-default-path` entries and absolute paths must keep being dropped. Not in this PR — it converts config inheritance into inheritance of executable repository code, which is a product decision rather than an implementation detail.

signals.title: dagql: reduce e-graph result-removal contention
signals.text: ## Motivation Removing a result from a wide output equivalence class repeatedly scanned the class's digests and result postings while holding `egraphMu`. Release and metadata-prune work therefore grew superlinearly as the class widened, increasing lock contention for unrelated cache operations. ## Design This change adds three cache-owned derived indexes: - an inverse output-equivalence-class-to-results index; - an exact per-result digest-posting index; and - an exact/broad posting classification for result cleanup. Newly published results record their exact digest postings. Imported results remain conservatively broad because the persistence schema does not contain exact result/term memberships. Broad imported cleanup therefore retains the safe class-posting scan; this change does not claim to remove that scan. The inverse output-class index replaces the separate deterministic class-wide survivor scan with an expiry-aware lookup over associated results. ## Correctness and compatibility Forward and inverse output-class associations are maintained as a pair across publication, merge, compaction, import, expiry, reset, and rollback. Merge and compaction canonicalize roots and rebuild the paired indexes together. Posting insertion and removal use a centralized exact/broad classification, and the survivor predicate preserves expiry behavior. Ownership counts, release cascades and callback order, lookup candidate membership, release/prune visibility, tracing and mutation order, prune cadence, and the `egraphMu` lock domain remain unchanged. Reset clears all three indexes with the e-graph. There is no persistence schema, version, migration, API, or user-visible semantic change. Import reconstructs result/output-equivalence-class associations and marks imported postings broad. Exact result/term associations remain unavailable after import, so the existing conservative class-scan fallback is preserved. No changie entry is included because this is internal derived bookkeeping with no user-facing API or semantic change. ## Scope and history The final merge diff is nine files: three production files, four focused correctness-test files, and two existing architecture documents. It contains the production optimization and its regression coverage, without benchmark infrastructure or a PR-only implementation plan. The eleven-commit branch history retains the reviewed empirical and planning work for provenance. The final `dagql: remove e-graph benchmark scaffolding` commit removes every benchmark-only test, fixture, observer, artifact helper, runner script, and benchmark/plan document from the merge tree. The two implementation commits remain separate conceptual review and rollback boundaries. ## Validation The final rebased head `8bfba77e77` passed: - `go test ./dagql -count=1` — 1.872s - `go test -race ./dagql -count=1` — 4.161s - the 14 focused affected DagQL tests — 0.865s - `dagger check golang:lint-all` - `dagger check markdown-lint:lint` - `dagger check golang:generate-all` - `dagger check markdown-lint:fix` - `gofmt` and `git diff --check` All eleven commits carry one matching DCO signoff. The rebased implementation commits retain the stable patch IDs of the reviewed originals, and the final production/docs patch is identical after removing benchmark-only instrumentation. The merge diff contains no generated/schema change. ## Paired benchmark evidence The measurements were collected with the reviewed development harness that is intentionally removed by the final cleanup commit. The measured production implementation is unchanged in the final merge diff; the evidence binds to that production behavior, not to final-tree or rebuilt-binary identity. - Transient wide release: R256 improved from 46.318 ms to 2.356 ms and R512 from 181.319 ms to 5.379 ms. The timing slope changed from 3.91x to 2.28x, while allocation scaling per doubling changed from 3.94x to 1.99x. - Persisted-fresh prune: R256 improved from 20.256 ms to 5.540 ms and R512 from 156.145 ms to 12.378 ms. The 12.6x R512 ratio and 7.709x baseline timing slope are host-specific, not expected production factors. The stronger structural result is allocation scaling per doubling changing from 3.86x to 1.98x. - Imported release R256 improved from 86.020 ms to 19.765 ms while retaining all 263,683 broad postings. Broad posting cleanup remains; the gain comes from removing the separate class-wide survivor scan. Allocations changed from 1,769,611 to 1,031. - The independent 50,000-result control produced candidate 317.357 ms, baseline 277.558 ms, and the one bounded candidate repeat 270.377 ms. No control regression was demonstrated at this measurement precision; none was excluded. Identical allocations/bytes, within-2% RSS, and matching fixture/posting/lock counters support treating the first candidate point as noise rather than claiming a speedup. Every process exited successfully, ran one exact sample, reported zero dropped observations, and preserved fixture, prune, and lock-counter populations. Only the allowed noisy control arm was repeated once. The same-host paired comparison was explicitly authorized because the original Linux VM was unstable. Host-specific timing factors are not production guarantees; the near-linear allocation scaling is the stronger evidence that the quadratic removal term is gone. Raw outputs and SHA-256 manifests are retained internally. ## Rollback and non-goals The two implementation commits are conceptual rollback boundaries: first the output-class inverse index, then exact posting tracking and cleanup. This slice does not add lock sharding, tombstones, asynchronous cleanup, persistence-schema changes, exact imported association persistence, ownership-semantic changes, imported read-path redesign, or broader e-graph optimization.

signals.title: fix: make `dagger module init` work from a subdirectory workspace
signals.text: Fixes #13889. When `dagger.toml` sits in a subdirectory instead of at the git root, `dagger module init` fails: ``` $ cd common && dagger module init go hello -y Error: sdk module init: failed to call sdk module initModule: workspace path .dagger/modules/hello is outside changeset root common ``` Passing `--path common/hello` avoids the error but splits the module in two: the engine writes `dagger-module.toml` under `common/hello/`, the SDK writes `main.go` under `hello/`. ## Why The workspace root is the git root, so a `dagger.toml` in a subdirectory means cwd is not the root. The engine resolves init paths against the root and applies the changeset there. SDKs stage their files against `Workspace.cwd`, because a changeset returned from a normal function call gets applied at the caller's cwd. Both are correct on their own. They only disagree when cwd isn't the root. ## Fix Both changes are engine-side; SDKs and the polyfill are untouched. - Pass the SDK a workspace with `cwd = "."` during `initModule` and `initClient`, so the cwd it stages against matches where the changeset actually lands. - Put the default module path next to the `dagger.toml` being edited instead of at the root, and record `[modules.<name>].source` relative to that config dir — the same conversion `dagger install` already does. Nothing changes for a workspace whose config is at the root. `--path` still means workspace-root-relative. The CLI help and the Go SDK docs now say so explicitly. ## Tests `TestGenerators/TestInitFromSubdirectoryWorkspace` covers module init, `--path` both inside and outside the caller's cwd, and client init, all from a subdirectory workspace. The fixture SDK now mirrors the polyfill's cwd rebasing, so it reproduces the real failure rather than a synthetic one — confirmed it fails without the fix.

signals.title: fix(workspace): make as-sdk paths consistently workspace-root-relative
signals.text: ## What `dagger.toml` carries two path conventions that only coincide when the config file sits at the workspace root: - `[modules.<name>].source` resolves against the **config directory** (`ResolveModuleEntrySource`). - `[[modules.<sdk>.as-sdk.modules]].path` is **workspace-root-relative**, everywhere it is read: module→SDK ownership (`sdkOwnersByModulePathFromConfig`), uninstall (`removeSDKManagedModuleReference`), the workspace SDK listing (`workspaceSDKFromEntry`), and `currentModule.asSDK.modules`, which the SDKs themselves consume (including the out-of-repo `dagger/go-sdk`). For instance (using #13890 ) ```toml [modules.my-module] source = ".dagger/modules/my-module" [[modules.dagger-go-sdk.as-sdk.modules]] path = "common/.dagger/modules/my-module" ``` While both are true, it feels a bad UX to have two paths not representing the same thing. By reading the toml file it's impossible to understand that `*.as-sdk.modules.path` is a workspace-root-relative one. `dagger module init` and `dagger api client init` already record the workspace-root-relative form — the example above is exactly what they write. `dagger setup` migration was the one writer anchoring as-sdk paths at the config directory instead, so this PR aligns it with the others and states the convention where the types are defined, including the published `dagger.toml` JSON schema. ## Is anything broken today? Not really, all that is working because the paths doesn't have the same meaning. It's more a question of being consistent. ## Tests - `core/schema` unit test pinning the anchor for a config planned below the workspace root. It is the only test that fails against the old writer; its comment is explicit that the shape is not reachable through `dagger setup` today. - `core/integration` assertions on the existing subdirectory-toolchains migration: the discovered toolchain is recorded by a workspace-root-relative path, and `dagger uninstall` resolves that path back to its as-sdk entry — end-to-end coverage of the contract in the monorepo layout. - Cross-checked against #13890, which is where the subdirectory `dagger module init` above becomes possible: with both branches applied, `TestGenerators/TestInitFromSubdirectoryWorkspace` passes unchanged, so the init writers and migration agree on the anchor.

signals.title: fix: classify dotted workspace-relative module refs as local
signals.text: `dagger api client init` fails on a module path with a dot in it: ```console $ dagger api client init go clients/api common/.dagger/mymod load module source: local path "common/.dagger/mymod" does not exist ``` You hit this from a subdirectory of a monorepo, where a module that is `.dagger/mymod` at the workspace root is `common/.dagger/mymod` relative to it. Adding `./` doesn't help: the ref is cleaned before it gets classified. ## Why `IsLocalRef` treated a ref as local if it started with `.` or `/`, or if it had no dot anywhere. The no-dot check was standing in for "is this a hostname". `common/.dagger/mymod` fails both, so it went to the git loader. Now it calls `gitref.FastKindCheck` (which already knows about pins, `./`, and the http/https/ssh schemes) and only looks for the host ahead of the first slash, like Go import paths do. Dot-free hosts still need a scheme, except scp-style (`git@internal:org/repo.git`) and Azure DevOps Server (`/_git/`). ## Also The same heuristic was copy-pasted in three other places, and they'd drifted: - `isLocalLegacyModuleRef` in `core/schema/modulesource.go`, used by `dagger update`: identical copy, deleted. - `workspaceAddressLooksRemote`: same bug, so `-W services/api.v2` was read as a git ref. - `isObviouslyRemoteWorkspaceRef`: already used the first-segment rule, just spelled out again. All three go through `IsLocalRef` now. `auth/registry.go` and `engine/vcs` also poke at dots but they answer different questions, so I left them alone. ## Known limitation `./mymod.v2` at the workspace root still reads as a git ref. The `./` is cleaned away and the cleaned form is what lands in `as-sdk.clients.module`, so the next load has nothing to go on. Fixing it means writing the `./` into the config, which is a format change, so not here. ## Tests `localref_test.go` covers the classifier. `TestAPIClientInitDottedModulePath` runs `client init` from a subdirectory against `common/.dagger/target`; both subtests fail without the fix, with the error above. CLI side has `TestIsObviouslyRemoteWorkspaceRef` plus a couple of new cases in `TestWorkspaceAddressLooksRemote`.

signals.title: fix: drop ReadHeaderTimeout on HTTP/2 servers
signals.text: Any dagger session that outlives 30 seconds currently dies with: ``` Error: Post "http://dagger/query": unexpected EOF ``` Reproduces on anything slow enough — no module or agent involved: ```console $ dagger core container from --address=alpine with-exec --args=sh,-c,'sleep 45; echo ok' stdout Error: Post "http://dagger/query": unexpected EOF # at 31.2s, deterministically ``` The engine logs nothing useful. From its side the client simply vanishes: three `client went away` lines for the telemetry streams, then session teardown. No panic, no crash, no restart. ## Cause `net/http` in **Go 1.26.6** now arms a connection-level read deadline from `ReadHeaderTimeout` *before* handing an unencrypted HTTP/2 connection off to the HTTP/2 server: ```go + if d := c.server.readHeaderTimeout(); d > 0 { + c.rwc.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(d)) + } protos := c.server.protocols() if c.tlsState == nil && protos.UnencryptedHTTP2() { if c.maybeServeUnencryptedHTTP2(ctx) { ``` The HTTP/2 server only disarms that deadline when `ReadTimeout > 0` (`h2_bundle.go`, `processHeaders`). None of our servers set `ReadTimeout`, so `ReadHeaderTimeout` silently became a hard cap on **connection lifetime**, independent of how active the connection is. A client multiplexes its GraphQL queries *and* its `/v1/traces|logs|metrics` streams over a single HTTP/2 connection, so when the deadline fires every stream dies at once — which is why one slow query takes down the whole session, and why the failure looks like an unexplained disconnect rather than a timeout. Reduced to a standalone program (h2c server + `http2.Transport`, handler sleeps 6s): | Go | `ReadHeaderTimeout` | result | | --- | --- | --- | | 1.26.6 | 3s | `unexpected EOF` at 3.0s | | 1.26.6 | 0 | ok at 6.0s | | 1.26.5 | 3s | ok at 6.0s | Confirmed by bisecting engines with one unchanged CLI binary: `dagger-engine-v1.0.0-beta.9` (built with go1.26.5) passes a 46s query; an engine built today (go1.26.6) fails at 30s. ## Why now Nothing in the repo changed. `engine/distconsts/consts.go` pins `GolangVersion = "1.26"` → `golang:1.26-alpine`, a floating minor tag, and `go.mod` has no `toolchain` directive. go1.26.6 was released 2026-08-11, so the first engine rebuild whose image cache missed after that date picked it up. That const used to carry a full patch pin (`1.25.5` → `1.25.6` → `1.25.7`, each an explicit CVE bump); #11843 dropped the patch component. Because the trigger is a cache miss on a floating tag, this lands at a different moment for each developer and CI runner, with no commit to blame. ## Fix Drop `ReadHeaderTimeout` from the three servers that enable unencrypted HTTP/2: - `cmd/engine/main.go` (30s) — the engine's client API - `engine/engineutil/executor_spec.go` (10s) — the nested-client API that module functions dial, so **any module function call outliving 10s** lost its engine connection - `internal/cmd/dagger/listen.go` (10s) — `dagger listen` sessions The latter two are latent versions of the same bug rather than what I was chasing, but they fail identically. ## Notes for review This forfeits the gosec **G112** slowloris guard on these three servers; the comments say so, and all three listen on local or otherwise trusted endpoints. Restoring the guard properly would mean implementing it as a listener wrapper that arms a timer on accept and cancels it on the first read, rather than as a connection deadline the HTTP/2 server never clears — happy to do that here instead if preferred. Re-pinning `GolangVersion` to a patch version is worth doing separately for reproducibility, but note it would neither have prevented this nor fix it; the change here is what fixes it, on any toolchain. ## Verification Rebuilt the dev engine with this patch: - a 60s query returns `ok` at 63.2s (was: `unexpected EOF` at 31.2s) - `dagger --env dev agent` reaches the prompt and stays healthy well past 30s, driven under a real pty

signals.title: feat: make workspace locking pinned by default
signals.text: ## Summary Make workspace locking automatic and pinned by default. - remove the `--lock` flag and hidden `dagger lock` command - keep `dagger update` as the explicit refresh command - introduce lockfile v2 without per-entry policies - continue reading v1 lockfiles for migration - always write new and updated lockfiles as v2 ## Why Lock policy is a property of how Dagger operates, not something that needs to be recorded independently for every lockfile entry. With pinned locking as the default, storing `"pin"` on every entry is redundant. Removing the lock modes from the CLI also gives workspaces one predictable behavior: reuse recorded values unless the user explicitly runs `dagger update`. ## Compatibility Dagger continues to read both lockfile v1 and v2. When reading a v1 lockfile: - `pin` entries retain their recorded values - `float` entries are refreshed once - the next write migrates the lockfile to v2 - the obsolete policy field is omitted from v2 output Unknown lockfile versions are rejected instead of being interpreted optimistically. Older Dagger releases that only understand v1 will reject v2 lockfiles. Using a new version is necessary because silently changing the v1 tuple shape would make compatibility failures ambiguous. ## Implementation notes Lockfile v2 changes an entry from: ```json ["namespace", "operation", ["inputs"], "value", "policy"] ``` to: ```json ["namespace", "operation", ["inputs"], "value"] ``` The legacy policy remains available in memory while reading and resolving v1 entries, but it is never serialized into v2. The active workspace lockfile is excluded from ambient host directory snapshots. This prevents automatic lockfile writes from changing directory digests. An explicit request to include the lockfile still takes precedence. ## Testing Completed: - `go test ./util/lockfile ./core/workspace ./core/schema` - focused core lockfile and workspace tests - focused internal CLI tests - integration package compilation - focused v1 float migration integration tests Still pending: - rerun the focused `dagger update` integration tests after the final explicit-include fix

signals.text: ## Summary - keep registry authentication session state out of container cache identity - execute each add/remove mutation without result caching so operation order is preserved - add cross-session cache coverage and private registry pull coverage ## Testing - original Go reproduction against the patched development engine - focused container registry tests: 8 passed - `dagger check golang:lint-all` - `dagger check test-split:test-container`: 657 passed; one unrelated proxy test failed when GitHub returned HTTP 503 Closes #13898.

signals.title: fix(container): preserve cache identity through registry auth
signals.text: ## Summary - keep registry authentication as session-local state without making it part of semantic container result identity - return the attached parent `ObjectResult` from `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth`, since they mutate ambient session auth rather than the container - conservatively allow `Container.from` to publish stable image content identity only for an untouched scratch container - cover cross-session cache reuse with auth both before and after `From`, plus constructor/clone defaults and modified-container `MultiFrom` preservation ## Problem Adding registry credentials to an otherwise unchanged container caused image pulls and downstream executions to miss cache across Dagger sessions. This was especially visible for the common sequence `container -> withRegistryAuth -> from(image) -> downstream operations`, even when the configured credentials were unrelated to the pulled image. The root cause was that the auth mutation was scoped correctly with `dagql.PerSessionInput`, but `dagql.Func` wrapped the unchanged Go container pointer in a new result whose identity included that session-local input. Session-local auth side effects were therefore coupled to semantic container result identity. ## Approach `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth` are now `NodeFunc`s that still execute against the current session's auth provider, but return the already-attached parent result. The e-graph can therefore treat the returned container as exactly the unchanged semantic value it is, allowing downstream cache reuse across sessions. `Container.from` no longer identifies the safe path by inspecting the parent field name. A newly constructed scratch container carries a private safety bit, while schema child cloning defaults it to false. This keeps stable image content identity available for untouched containers while conservatively preserving call identity for genuinely modified containers whose state survives `From`. This takes a different approach from the now-closed #13899: it retains normal per-session caching and restores result equivalence instead of marking registry-auth operations `DoNotCache`. ## Validation - `go test ./core ./core/schema -count=1` - `dagger api call engine-dev test --pkg ./core/integration --run='^TestContainer/(TestMultiFrom|TestWithRegistryAuth.*)$'` — 8 passed - `git diff --check` - `dagger generate -y` — `dagger-go-sdk:generate` passed; the overall run was blocked in the unrelated Elixir generator because the BEAM runtime aborted with `OS monotonic time stepped backwards` (exit 134); no generated changes were produced - `dagger check '*:lint'` — Helm, Java, Markdown, and Python passed; `elixir-client:lint` hit the same BEAM host-clock abort Closes #13898.

signals.title: [backport-0.21] fix(container): preserve cache identity through registry auth
signals.text: ## Summary Backports #13901 to the v0.21 maintenance line for v0.21.9. Registry authentication remains session-local, but `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth` now return the attached parent result instead of coupling ambient auth side effects to semantic container identity. This restores downstream cache reuse across sessions when auth is applied before or after `Container.from`. `Container.from` also retains the source fix's conservative safety state: untouched scratch containers can publish stable image content identity, while genuinely modified containers preserve their call identity. This addresses the v0.21.x behavior reported in #13898. ## Source provenance - Source PR: https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/13901 - Main merge commit: https://github.com/dagger/dagger/commit/06aee1f521bd84d84f6ba76d237ab5e2f3e7a73e - Source implementation commit: https://github.com/dagger/dagger/commit/f07d62dbd0c723c23d7b5fee594e381df032cab7 - Source release-note commit: https://github.com/dagger/dagger/commit/738a73717d4b24404f89e7b42359169deb334351 - Applied with `cherry-pick -x -s` as `243a3631e77ee27bc29dd74f2d9f514f18030a82` and `91f653ce333bfb2cd046a272f8470a4fbc6561ce` ## v0.21 adaptation No adaptation was required. Both source commits cherry-picked cleanly onto `upstream/backport-0.21` at `67425bb6379a6588564d2194a766b31fde5e865c`. The maintenance branch already contains the required `NodeFunc`, `PerSessionInput`, attached `ObjectResult`, schema-child clone, and `From` content-digest machinery. The two backport commits have the same stable patch IDs as their source commits, and the final delta remains the exact six-file source change: 128 insertions and 23 deletions. ## Validation Passed: - `go test ./core ./core/schema -count=1` - `dagger call engine-dev test --pkg='./core/integration' --run='^TestContainer/(TestMultiFrom|TestWithRegistryAuth|TestWithRegistryAuthDoesNotInvalidateCache)$'` — 6 passed, trace `a8e85bdb40ef9653a3d02bc7d2f57fc5` - `dagger -m ./toolchains/go call --source=. lint-module --module=core` — trace `f8d55258f1fb0cacac6ad7f624154d4c` - `gofmt -d` on all changed Go files - `git diff --check upstream/backport-0.21...HEAD` - Stable patch-ID comparison against both source commits Local environment limitations preserved for remote CI verification: - `dagger generate -y` produced no generated changes, but the broad workspace run was blocked by v1-CLI/v0.21 module API incompatibilities (`LLM.History*` and `CurrentWorkspace`) and the host BEAM `OS monotonic time stepped backwards` abort; trace `f91fb9fffcc3b497bdde175364e1e19b`. - The broad `dagger check '*:lint'` entrypoint stopped while loading the same incompatible release module before any lint ran; the scoped core lint above passed. - The pre-existing `TestWithRegistryAuthAfterAnonymousBearerPull` was attempted twice but failed while starting its nested dev-engine tunnel with `unexpected EOF`, before any registry-auth operation ran; traces `0fc8022d0db0a0778a813aab5d7532d4` and `2967ee131baafc7493880c628a64ab2d`. ## Release note Carries the exact source `Fixed` entry at `.changes/unreleased/Fixed-20260814-203258.yaml`, attributed to source PR #13901.

signals.title: fix: accept @ and # in git refs
signals.text: Git refs used different separators depending on where they appeared: - Module sources accepted `@ref`, but not `#ref`. - Git-backed directory and file arguments accepted `#ref`, but not `@ref`. This PR makes both forms work everywhere. Users can now write either separator in `dagger.toml` module sources and in directory or file settings, and copy a Git URL between them without changing it. Includes a workspace regression test that loads a module source using `#ref` and reads a directory setting using `@ref`. signal.title: Clean up tests for the Go client library
signal.text: ## Problem To test the Go client library, we built a custom test harness. That harness only runs in GitHub Actions; it relies heavily on single-use glue code; and it jams together testing dimensions that should be decoupled. Concretely: the `TestProvision` test is wired into `publish.yml` and only runs on pushes to main and tags, never on a PR. The rest of the suite runs through `go-sdk-dev`, a Dagger module built only to call `go test`. And one suite does three jobs at once — bootstrap the CLI, start an engine, test the client — so a developer with plain `go test` can't run any of it. ## Solution Turn them into ordinary Go tests. The engine-dependent tests move to `sdk/go/e2e`, a normal Go module which can be tested by `go test`, either called directly by the user, or orchestrated by a generic Dagger module such as `github.com/dagger/go`. | Dependency | Before | After | | -- | -- | -- | | Github Actions | required 🔴 | not required 🟢 | | Single-use Dagger module | required 🔴 | not required 🟢 | | Run with native `go test` | not supported 🔴 | supported 🟢 | - `sdk/go` holds unit tests with no engine dependency, and pre-existing documentation examples. - `sdk/go/e2e` holds two e2e test suites: `TestBootstrap` (the library downloads and runs a CLI), and `TestAgainstEngines` (call the library against a matrix of engines) ## Task list > **TL;DR:** `sdk/go/e2e`'s `TestBootstrap` and `TestAgainstEngines` both fail during their shared harness setup. The nested Dagger client detects the container's projected filesystem as its workspace instead of inheriting the caller's workspace. - [ ] Fix both tests by implementing [#13054](https://github.com/dagger/dagger/issues/13054).

signal.title: sdk(improvement): support nullable object returns
signal.text: #### What Support nullable GraphQL object results in generated clients and built-in module SDKs. The motivating API is `GitRepository.latestVersion`: a repository may have no stable semantic-version tag, so callers need a real missing value and can choose a fallback. ```go version, err := repo.LatestVersion(ctx) if err != nil { return err } if version == nil { version = repo.Head() } ``` #### Generated clients Nullable object methods now query the object's ID before returning. A missing ID becomes the language's native empty value; a present ID rebuilds the object client. Non-null object fields stay lazy, and scalar and list methods do not change. This produces `nil` in Go, `null` in TypeScript, PHP, and .NET, `None` or `Option` in Python and Rust, `Optional` in Java, and `{:ok, value | nil}` in Elixir. #### Module functions Module authors can also declare nullable object returns: - TypeScript: `Promise<User | null>` - PHP: `?Directory` - Java: `Optional<Directory>` - Go: `dagger.Nullable[*dagger.Directory]` Python and Dang already had nullable syntax. This also completes Elixir's existing `Object.t() | nil` path by registering and encoding optional object results correctly. #### Compatibility and tests Generated templates receive the schema version and keep the old lazy method shape before `v1.0.0-beta.10`. From beta.10 onward, nullable object methods use the new eager nullable result. This preserves modules pinned to older schemas without adding runtime compatibility code. Generator tests cover both sides of the version boundary. Runtime integration tests exercise both a present object and `null` for Go, TypeScript, PHP, Java, Python, and Elixir. Focused SDK tests and lint pass locally with the pinned beta.10 release.

signal.title: dagql: reduce e-graph result-removal contention
signal.text: ## Motivation Removing a result from a wide output equivalence class repeatedly scanned the class's digests and result postings while holding `egraphMu`. Release and metadata-prune work therefore grew superlinearly as the class widened, increasing lock contention for unrelated cache operations. ## Design This change adds three cache-owned derived indexes: - an inverse output-equivalence-class-to-results index; - an exact per-result digest-posting index; and - an exact/broad posting classification for result cleanup. Newly published results record their exact digest postings. Imported results remain conservatively broad because the persistence schema does not contain exact result/term memberships. Broad imported cleanup therefore retains the safe class-posting scan; this change does not claim to remove that scan. The inverse output-class index replaces the separate deterministic class-wide survivor scan with an expiry-aware lookup over associated results. ## Correctness and compatibility Forward and inverse output-class associations are maintained as a pair across publication, merge, compaction, import, expiry, reset, and rollback. Merge and compaction canonicalize roots and rebuild the paired indexes together. Posting insertion and removal use a centralized exact/broad classification, and the survivor predicate preserves expiry behavior. Ownership counts, release cascades and callback order, lookup candidate membership, release/prune visibility, tracing and mutation order, prune cadence, and the `egraphMu` lock domain remain unchanged. Reset clears all three indexes with the e-graph. There is no persistence schema, version, migration, API, or user-visible semantic change. Import reconstructs result/output-equivalence-class associations and marks imported postings broad. Exact result/term associations remain unavailable after import, so the existing conservative class-scan fallback is preserved. No changie entry is included because this is internal derived bookkeeping with no user-facing API or semantic change. ## Scope and history The final merge diff is nine files: three production files, four focused correctness-test files, and two existing architecture documents. It contains the production optimization and its regression coverage, without benchmark infrastructure or a PR-only implementation plan. The eleven-commit branch history retains the reviewed empirical and planning work for provenance. The final `dagql: remove e-graph benchmark scaffolding` commit removes every benchmark-only test, fixture, observer, artifact helper, runner script, and benchmark/plan document from the merge tree. The two implementation commits remain separate conceptual review and rollback boundaries. ## Validation The final rebased head `8bfba77e77` passed: - `go test ./dagql -count=1` — 1.872s - `go test -race ./dagql -count=1` — 4.161s - the 14 focused affected DagQL tests — 0.865s - `dagger check golang:lint-all` - `dagger check markdown-lint:lint` - `dagger check golang:generate-all` - `dagger check markdown-lint:fix` - `gofmt` and `git diff --check` All eleven commits carry one matching DCO signoff. The rebased implementation commits retain the stable patch IDs of the reviewed originals, and the final production/docs patch is identical after removing benchmark-only instrumentation. The merge diff contains no generated/schema change. ## Paired benchmark evidence The measurements were collected with the reviewed development harness that is intentionally removed by the final cleanup commit. The measured production implementation is unchanged in the final merge diff; the evidence binds to that production behavior, not to final-tree or rebuilt-binary identity. - Transient wide release: R256 improved from 46.318 ms to 2.356 ms and R512 from 181.319 ms to 5.379 ms. The timing slope changed from 3.91x to 2.28x, while allocation scaling per doubling changed from 3.94x to 1.99x. - Persisted-fresh prune: R256 improved from 20.256 ms to 5.540 ms and R512 from 156.145 ms to 12.378 ms. The 12.6x R512 ratio and 7.709x baseline timing slope are host-specific, not expected production factors. The stronger structural result is allocation scaling per doubling changing from 3.86x to 1.98x. - Imported release R256 improved from 86.020 ms to 19.765 ms while retaining all 263,683 broad postings. Broad posting cleanup remains; the gain comes from removing the separate class-wide survivor scan. Allocations changed from 1,769,611 to 1,031. - The independent 50,000-result control produced candidate 317.357 ms, baseline 277.558 ms, and the one bounded candidate repeat 270.377 ms. No control regression was demonstrated at this measurement precision; none was excluded. Identical allocations/bytes, within-2% RSS, and matching fixture/posting/lock counters support treating the first candidate point as noise rather than claiming a speedup. Every process exited successfully, ran one exact sample, reported zero dropped observations, and preserved fixture, prune, and lock-counter populations. Only the allowed noisy control arm was repeated once. The same-host paired comparison was explicitly authorized because the original Linux VM was unstable. Host-specific timing factors are not production guarantees; the near-linear allocation scaling is the stronger evidence that the quadratic removal term is gone. Raw outputs and SHA-256 manifests are retained internally. ## Rollback and non-goals The two implementation commits are conceptual rollback boundaries: first the output-class inverse index, then exact posting tracking and cleanup. This slice does not add lock sharding, tombstones, asynchronous cleanup, persistence-schema changes, exact imported association persistence, ownership-semantic changes, imported read-path redesign, or broader e-graph optimization.

signal.title: fix: classify dotted workspace-relative module refs as local
signal.text: `dagger api client init` fails on a module path with a dot in it: ```console $ dagger api client init go clients/api common/.dagger/mymod load module source: local path "common/.dagger/mymod" does not exist ``` You hit this from a subdirectory of a monorepo, where a module that is `.dagger/mymod` at the workspace root is `common/.dagger/mymod` relative to it. Adding `./` doesn't help: the ref is cleaned before it gets classified. ## Why `IsLocalRef` treated a ref as local if it started with `.` or `/`, or if it had no dot anywhere. The no-dot check was standing in for "is this a hostname". `common/.dagger/mymod` fails both, so it went to the git loader. Now it calls `gitref.FastKindCheck` (which already knows about pins, `./`, and the http/https/ssh schemes) and only looks for the host ahead of the first slash, like Go import paths do. Dot-free hosts still need a scheme, except scp-style (`git@internal:org/repo.git`) and Azure DevOps Server (`/_git/`). ## Also The same heuristic was copy-pasted in three other places, and they'd drifted: - `isLocalLegacyModuleRef` in `core/schema/modulesource.go`, used by `dagger update`: identical copy, deleted. - `workspaceAddressLooksRemote`: same bug, so `-W services/api.v2` was read as a git ref. - `isObviouslyRemoteWorkspaceRef`: already used the first-segment rule, just spelled out again. All three go through `IsLocalRef` now. `auth/registry.go` and `engine/vcs` also poke at dots but they answer different questions, so I left them alone. ## Known limitation `./mymod.v2` at the workspace root still reads as a git ref. The `./` is cleaned away and the cleaned form is what lands in `as-sdk.clients.module`, so the next load has nothing to go on. Fixing it means writing the `./` into the config, which is a format change, so not here. ## Tests `localref_test.go` covers the classifier. `TestAPIClientInitDottedModulePath` runs `client init` from a subdirectory against `common/.dagger/target`; both subtests fail without the fix, with the error above. CLI side has `TestIsObviouslyRemoteWorkspaceRef` plus a couple of new cases in `TestWorkspaceAddressLooksRemote`.

signal.title: workspace: compare changes from an explicit baseline
signal.text: This completes the engine API needed to remove `dagger/polyfill`. The caller now keeps the workspace it received, generates files on a new immutable workspace value, then compares the two: ```text before = disk + existing edits after = moduleSource.generate(before) # before + generated files after.changes(from: before) # generated files only ``` `ModuleSource.generate(workspace)` returns a `Workspace`, so SDKs can compose generation with normal workspace edits. `Workspace.changes(from:)` performs the comparison only when a `Changeset` is required and returns paths relative to the workspace cwd. This avoids a separate `WorkspaceDiff` type and avoids a `fork()` lifecycle that callers could forget. The baseline is an ordinary immutable workspace value already available to the caller. It also handles module initialization correctly: the SDK sees the staged module scaffold, but returns only the files it generated. `ModuleSource.generateLocalDependencies` remains temporarily because released SDKs still call it. signal.title: 🐞 `withRegistryAuth` invalidates image and execution caches across sessions
signal.text: ### What is the issue? `Container.withRegistryAuth` changes the cache identity of an otherwise unchanged container. Image pulls and downstream executions then miss the cache across Dagger sessions. Registry credentials are session state and are not stored in `core.Container`. Therefore, adding credentials should not change the container filesystem or invalidate downstream execution cache entries. The problem occurs even when the configured registry address is unrelated to the image being pulled: ```go client.Container(). WithRegistryAuth("registry.example.com", "anyuser", secret). From("alpine:3.20"). WithExec(...) ``` The same execution without `WithRegistryAuth` is cached across sessions. The authenticated branch runs again and produces a different random value. This reproduces with Dagger v0.21.8, v1.0.0-beta.9, and current `main` at `b068d8a7b`. The original user report is in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/707636530424053791/1488136596237713459/1537636243314049065). #### Expected `withRegistryAuth` registers credentials in the current session without changing the identity of the returned container. If the resolved image digest and execution inputs are unchanged, image and execution cache entries should be reusable across sessions. #### Actual The authenticated branch has a different identity in every session. The digest-qualified `Container.from` operation runs instead of reporting `CACHED`, a nested pull span appears, and downstream `withExec` runs again. #### Root cause `withRegistryAuth` is registered with `dagql.PerSessionInput`. Its resolver mutates the session authentication provider and returns the unchanged Go container pointer. However, `dagql.Func` wraps that pointer in a new result whose recipe contains the session ID. That session-scoped result becomes the receiver of `Container.from` and all later operations. It also prevents the canonical `From` path from assigning its stable image content identity because the direct parent call is `withRegistryAuth`, not the bare `container` call. The behavior was introduced by `3fde468ad` and first appeared in v0.21.1. That change fixed a real problem where the authentication side effect could be skipped in a new session, but it coupled session-local side-effect execution to the semantic identity of the returned container. `withoutRegistryAuth` has the same identity and mutable-side-effect concerns. #### Suggested fix Treat `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth` as non-cacheable session operations while returning the attached parent container result. This keeps explicit credential mutations ordered and ensures that registry authentication does not become part of the container identity. ### Dagger version ```text dagger v0.21.8 (image://registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.8) linux/amd64 ``` Also reproduced with: ```text client-version=v1.0.0-beta.9 server-version=v1.0.0-beta.9+1c6e07b1 ``` ### Steps to reproduce Create a Go program using `dagger.io/dagger v0.21.8`: ```go package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" "strings" "dagger.io/dagger" ) func main() { ctx := context.Background() client, err := dagger.Connect(ctx, dagger.WithLogOutput(os.Stderr)) if err != nil { panic(err) } defer client.Close() stamp := []string{"sh", "-c", "cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid > /stamp; cat /stamp"} control := client.Container(). From("alpine:3.20"). WithExec(stamp) bug := client.Container(). WithRegistryAuth( "registry.example.com", "anyuser", client.SetSecret("s", "dummy"), ). From("alpine:3.20"). WithExec(stamp) controlStamp, err := control.File("/stamp").Contents(ctx) if err != nil { panic(err) } bugStamp, err := bug.File("/stamp").Contents(ctx) if err != nil { panic(err) } fmt.Println("CONTROL", strings.TrimSpace(controlStamp)) fmt.Println("BUG ", strings.TrimSpace(bugStamp)) } ``` Run it in two separate sessions: ```shell go mod init registry-auth-cache-repro go get dagger.io/dagger@v0.21.8 go run . go run . ``` To test v1.0.0-beta.9, add this connection option and run the program directly: ```go dagger.WithEnvironmentVariable("DAGGER_X_RELEASE", "v1.0.0-beta.9") ``` ### Log output ```text Session 1 CONTROL 3c58afe2-abf3-4aa3-90a3-ec5c0f381c70 BUG cb70c53c-12ae-413a-9b16-892d34178fbd Session 2 CONTROL 3c58afe2-abf3-4aa3-90a3-ec5c0f381c70 BUG 10087caa-e917-4062-aebe-f761d87a14be ``` Verbose spans show the difference: ```text # Control branch Container.from CACHED Container.withExec CACHED # withRegistryAuth branch, in both sessions pulling docker.io/library/alpine:3.20@sha256:... DONE Container.from DONE Container.withExec DONE ```

signal.title: fix(container): preserve cache identity through registry auth
signal.text: ## Summary - keep registry authentication as session-local state without making it part of semantic container result identity - return the attached parent `ObjectResult` from `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth`, since they mutate ambient session auth rather than the container - conservatively allow `Container.from` to publish stable image content identity only for an untouched scratch container - cover cross-session cache reuse with auth both before and after `From`, plus constructor/clone defaults and modified-container `MultiFrom` preservation ## Problem Adding registry credentials to an otherwise unchanged container caused image pulls and downstream executions to miss cache across Dagger sessions. This was especially visible for the common sequence `container -> withRegistryAuth -> from(image) -> downstream operations`, even when the configured credentials were unrelated to the pulled image. The root cause was that the auth mutation was scoped correctly with `dagql.PerSessionInput`, but `dagql.Func` wrapped the unchanged Go container pointer in a new result whose identity included that session-local input. Session-local auth side effects were therefore coupled to semantic container result identity. ## Approach `withRegistryAuth` and `withoutRegistryAuth` are now `NodeFunc`s that still execute against the current session's auth provider, but return the already-attached parent result. The e-graph can therefore treat the returned container as exactly the unchanged semantic value it is, allowing downstream cache reuse across sessions. `Container.from` no longer identifies the safe path by inspecting the parent field name. A newly constructed scratch container carries a private safety bit, while schema child cloning defaults it to false. This keeps stable image content identity available for untouched containers while conservatively preserving call identity for genuinely modified containers whose state survives `From`. This takes a different approach from the now-closed #13899: it retains normal per-session caching and restores result equivalence instead of marking registry-auth operations `DoNotCache`. ## Validation - `go test ./core ./core/schema -count=1` - `dagger api call engine-dev test --pkg ./core/integration --run='^TestContainer/(TestMultiFrom|TestWithRegistryAuth.*)$'` — 8 passed - `git diff --check` - `dagger generate -y` — `dagger-go-sdk:generate` passed; the overall run was blocked in the unrelated Elixir generator because the BEAM runtime aborted with `OS monotonic time stepped backwards` (exit 134); no generated changes were produced - `dagger check '*:lint'` — Helm, Java, Markdown, and Python passed; `elixir-client:lint` hit the same BEAM host-clock abort Closes #13898.
